also: if you need to stay on

evidence: Plaut. As. 597: quīn tū hīc manēs?
Cic. Att. 8.3.7: in Ītaliā fortasse manēbitur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of staying where one is: at home, in a place, with someone (apud aliquem). With an adjective, of staying in a state: clausae fenestrae manent, the shutters stay shut (Plin. Ep. 9.36.1). The imperative manē is “wait!”.

evidence: Cic. Att. 7.14.3: mulierēs nostrae praeter cēterās Rōmae remānsērunt
terms.comment: Of those who stay when others leave.

terms.gloss: stay on, stay for a while
terms.comment: Cicero’s word for stopping somewhere on a journey, or staying longer than planned.

evidence: Cic. Sen. 22: modo permaneat studium et industria
terms.comment: Of what lasts or holds out.

phrases.latin: Quō nunc abīs? quīn tū hīc manēs?
phrases.english: Where are you off to now? Why don’t you stay here?

phrases.latin: signifer, statue signum; hīc manēbimus optimē
phrases.english: standard-bearer, plant the standard: this is the best place for us to stay

sources: Lewis & Short: maneo · Lewis & Short: remaneo · Lewis & Short: commoror · Lewis & Short: permaneo
